-84.38558,33.75103.name: High Containment Core (HCC) (formerly the Viral Immunology Center)
-84.38558,33.75103.state: 100 Piedmont Avenue SE, Atlanta, GA 30303, United States
-84.38558,33.75103.desc: A BSL4 animal laboratory, operational. Run by Georgia State University. It is categorised as a university laboratory, working on human health. Personnel work in both pressure suits and sealed cabinets. Containment space: 60 SqM. Operational or announced: 1988. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

175.31000,-37.79000.name: Livestock Improvement Corporation
175.31000,-37.79000.desc: A New Zealand farmer-owned cooperative supplying dairy genetics to most of the national herd, and running the genomic evaluation the herd is bred on. Cooperative ownership does not slow the genetics: an index change here reaches almost every dairy cow in the country within a few generations, which suggests the speed is set by the technology rather than by who owns the company.

-117.20100,32.89900.name: Element Biosciences
-117.20100,32.89900.desc: A sequencing company competing with Illumina, part of the first real challenge to that dominance in over a decade. Competition in sequencing instruments changes the cost of checking things, which affects everyone doing verification rather than production.

116.43000,39.92000.name: Chinese state agricultural investment — seed industry revitalisation
116.43000,39.92000.state: Beijing — Ministry of Agriculture, 11 Nongzhanguan Nanli
116.43000,39.92000.desc: State-directed consolidation of Chinese seed companies into a smaller number of national champions, through Sinochem, COFCO and provincial funds. The stated aim is seed self-sufficiency: China imports a large share of its maize and soy genetics and treats that as a strategic exposure. Consolidation here is industrial policy, where the same concentration elsewhere is the residue of private mergers.

-122.29000,37.87000.name: Caribou Biosciences
-122.29000,37.87000.desc: Founded by Jennifer Doudna, and the company through which the Berkeley side of the CRISPR patent dispute licensed its intellectual property. It holds a foundational position and lost the interference proceedings, which is why the licensing estate everyone else pays into sits with the Broad instead — the science was shared, the rights were not.

-83.02000,40.00000.name: Ohio State / land-grant agricultural extension
-83.02000,40.00000.desc: The US land-grant extension system is how public agricultural research reaches farmers as advice rather than as a sales call. Its funding has fallen for decades while input companies have expanded their own agronomy services, so the advice a farmer receives now comes increasingly from whoever is selling the input. That shift is quiet, documented in budget lines, and shapes adoption more than any regulator does.

149.12450,-35.30800.name: Australia Group
149.12450,-35.30800.desc: An informal arrangement of 43 states that harmonises export controls on pathogens, toxins and the equipment to work with them. Informal is accurate: it has no treaty and no secretariat of its own, and it is the main practical brake on where dangerous biological material can be sent.

-106.54000,35.05200.name: Sandia National Laboratories — biodetection
-106.54000,35.05200.state: Albuquerque, New Mexico — Kirtland Air Force Base
-106.54000,35.05200.desc: Builds engineered biological sensors for detecting pathogens and chemical agents, under nuclear-weapons-laboratory management. A detector that works by using a living system is itself a modified organism, and defence laboratories are where most of that work is funded.

-77.43400,37.54100.name: United Network for Organ Sharing
-77.43400,37.54100.desc: Runs the US transplant waiting list, on which around a hundred thousand people sit and several thousand die each year. That queue is the argument for engineered pig organs, and it is also what will decide who receives the first of them — an allocation system built for human donors now has to rank patients for an organ from an animal.

6.14200,46.21000.name: Sidley Austin — Geneva trade practice
6.14200,46.21000.desc: Advises on WTO disputes over agricultural biotechnology, including the case brought against the EU’s approval moratorium. Trade law is the route by which one country’s biosafety rules become another country’s problem, and it is argued by a small number of firms.

8.64000,49.89000.name: Demeter International
8.64000,49.89000.desc: Certifies biodynamic production to standards stricter than organic, including on seed: varieties bred by methods it rejects cannot be used at all, and that includes cell fusion techniques the organic rules permit. Where organic excludes engineered material from the field, this excludes it from the breeding history of the variety.

-77.17400,38.87900.name: Fish and Wildlife Service — permits for releases into wild populations
-77.17400,38.87900.state: Falls Church, Virginia — US Fish and Wildlife Service
-77.17400,38.87900.desc: Putting an animal into a wild population needs a permit from the wildlife agency, separate from anything a biosafety regulator says. That covers engineered insects intended to suppress a wild population, and anything proposed for conservation — an engineered chestnut, a resistant ferret, a drive against island predators. The agency’s question is about the wild population rather than about the technology, and it is a question local knowledge can answer.
